quiz.question: What makes a file a "module" in TypeScript?

answers.answer: It must be inside a special modules folder
It contains at least one export or import statement
It must have the .module.ts file extension
It must be registered in a configuration file

quiz.explanation: A file becomes a module when it contains an export or import statement. This is what distinguishes a module from a plain script file.

quiz.question: What happens to variables declared inside a module?

answers.answer: They are automatically available to all other files
They are only accessible within that module unless explicitly exported
They are shared globally across the entire project
They must be declared with a special keyword to stay private

quiz.explanation: Each module has its own scope. Variables stay private to the module by default and are only visible to other files when explicitly exported. This prevents accidental name collisions.
